raw_response:
I would evaluate **NLog first and Apache log4net second**. Both offer the SQL-plus-local-file arrangement you described and accept an exception object directly. They are logging libraries you integrate into the existing C#/WPF application.

## 1. NLog

[NLog](https://nlog-project.org/) is the first alternative I would try. Its documented targets include files and databases, and the same event can be sent to multiple destinations. That matches the shape of your requirement: keep a local file target enabled alongside the database target.

For SQL output, [DatabaseTarget](https://nlog-project.org/documentation/v6.0.0/html/T_NLog_Targets_DatabaseTarget.htm) uses an ADO.NET provider and configurable SQL commands and parameters. The documentation inspected here places it in the NLog.Database assembly. You still need a compatible database provider, connection settings, a table, and the mapping from event fields to SQL parameters.

For the exception itself, the [Error(Exception, String) API](https://nlog-project.org/documentation/v6.0.0/html/M_NLog_Logger_Error_3.htm) lets application code pass the exception as an object:

```csharp
logger.Error(ex, "Saving the record failed");
```

You therefore do not have to break an exception into separate properties at every call site. Select an output layout that includes the exception information you want retained. Database-column mapping is still configuration work; accepting an exception object does not automatically design your SQL table.

NLog's overview lists .NET Framework and modern .NET support. Your exact target framework is unspecified, so check the chosen NLog and database-provider package versions against the WPF project's target framework.

## 2. Apache log4net

[Apache log4net's AdoNetAppender](https://logging.apache.org/log4net/manual/configuration/appenders/adonetappender.html) documents database logging, including a SQL Server configuration with parameterized inserts and an ExceptionLayout for the exception column. Pair that with [RollingFileAppender](https://logging.apache.org/log4net/manual/configuration/appenders/rollingfileappender.html) for local files with size- or date-based rotation. Its [FAQ](https://logging.apache.org/log4net/log4net-2.0.8/release/faq.html) confirms that a logger can have multiple output appenders.

The [ILog.Error(Object, Exception) API](https://logging.apache.org/log4net/log4net-2.0.8/release/sdk/html/M_log4net_ILog_Error_1.htm) takes the exception directly and includes its stack trace:

```csharp
log.Error("Saving the record failed", ex);
```

This is a concrete second option if its logger/appender configuration model suits your application. The current [framework support table](https://logging.apache.org/log4net/manual/supported-frameworks.html) lists the relevant database and file appenders for .NET Framework 4.6.2 and .NET Standard 2.0. That is evidence for those documented targets, not a blanket promise for every historical .NET version.

## Configuration point that matters for your SQL-error case

Configure the local file as an independently enabled destination, alongside SQL logging. Do not make producing the only local diagnostic depend on a successful database insert. This is an implementation recommendation based on the documented multiple-destination facilities, not a claim that I have tested your application.

During evaluation, deliberately cause the application's database operation to fail and confirm that the exception still reaches the local log. Also test an unavailable logging database. Check the chosen path's write permission, exception layout, buffering, and shutdown behavior. The log4net FAQ explicitly describes delivery as best effort; neither the documents inspected nor this review establish lossless delivery during crashes or storage failure.

I would keep your existing Serilog experience as the comparison baseline and make the decision from a small NLog-versus-log4net trial using those failure cases. I have not established Python support for either recommendation, and I have treated it as the optional benefit you described.

**Evidence limits:** This is a documentation-based shortlist, not an executed integration. The question is dated January 10, 2023; several accessible sources are undated live manuals, and the NLog API pages describe version 6.0, which is later than that decision date. These sources establish the documented capabilities of the versions shown; they do not reconstruct every package/version combination available on the original question date.
